If this were my problem, either reply would serve equally well because both are technically rigorous, comprehensive, and cover the exact same core protocol concepts without error. Both explain that TCP must synchronize two independent sequence spaces (four logical steps compressed into three via SYN-ACK), that a two-way handshake leaves the server without confirmation of its own ISN, and that the third packet is necessary to prevent stale duplicate SYNs from establishing half-open connections. Both also correctly explore simultaneous opens, the Two Generals problem, SYN floods/cookies, teardown, and modern adaptations like TFO and QUIC.
